name: Scrapwall Weld-Visor MK-2 (Acid Cut)
description:
Salvaged from decommissioned Crucible fab-floor stock, this half-visor is a patchwork of welded scrap steel, heat-warped polycarbonate lenses, and stripped rubber gasket trim. The lens is a yellowed amber—scratched but functional—held in a bent steel frame secured with mismatched bolts and electrical tape. Edges are ground smooth enough not to cut. Paint is gone in layers, showing rust-brown, safety orange, and bare metal beneath.

Worn low on the face, it shields against acid-rain splash and airborne grit. The nose bridge is padded with cut foam salvaged from a transit seat. No electronics, no filters—just physical barrier between a Shelf worker's face and the air.
functionality: Provides basic physical protection against acid-rain splash, debris, and airborne particulate. No filtration. Adjustable strap tension via a knotted cord. Fits over most face shapes including those with minor cranial chrome.
what_it_says: You built your own protection because no one sold you any.
story_hooks: The visor's frame is stamped with a Crucible lot number — tracing it leads to a decommissioned fab-floor that officially never existed.
A Shelf kid wearing one identical to this was the last person seen near the body — but the tape color is wrong.
A market fabricator is quietly selling these with a thin hidden pocket in the foam pad, used for smuggling data chips.
